title.narrative: Addressing climate vulnerabilities through enhancing biodiversity and seed sovereignty

description.narrative:
'Nayakrishi' is a biodiversity-based farming method, actively practised by 150,000 farmers in the 9 target districts. Since 1992, the Nayakrishi movement has mobilised small-scale farmers to enhance the diversity of crops and apply alternatives to the chemical and mechanical agricultural methods that characterise industrial food production. This approach focuses on promoting the preservation, regeneration and sharing of local seed varieties among local farming communities, especially women, who want to preserve traditional seed varieties at threat from the promotion of market-oriented varieties.
As the impacts of climate change are increasingly manifest in rural Bangladeshi communities, Nayakrishi farmers are aware of the need to enhance their capacity to collect and distribute seeds among themselves to compensate for crop losses. In UBINIG's working areas, 70% of farmers are affected by weather conditions unfavourable for growing crops.
This project will address these vulnerabilities and opportunities for change by delivering training on sustainable Nayakrishi principles and approaches (at the village level and through Training of Trainers at UBINIG centres); facilitating Farmer Field Schools (FFS) to promote mutual learning among farmers, especially relating to adaptation to climate change and adverse weather conditions; enhancing seed collection, regeneration and exchange among farmers, especially at times of crisis and crop failure, through the Nayakrishi seed network; holding an annual farmers' conference and biodiversity festival; engaging with members of women and biodiversity networks through additional training; and building effective mechanisms to market Nayakrishi farmers' products, linking farmers and conscious consumers.
